kept.q: Choose the option with the correct order of adjectives to complete the sentence: Mr. Adeyemi bought a ______ table for his new office in Lagos.
kept.explanation: In English, adjectives usually follow the order: opinion, size, material. 'Beautiful' is opinion, 'large' is size, and 'wooden' is material, so this order is correct.
kept.pidgin: For English, adjective dey follow order: opinion, size, material. 'Beautiful' na opinion, 'large' na size, 'wooden' na material, so this order correct well well.

kept.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Ngozi ______ attends the morning assembly because she lives very far from the school.
kept.explanation: The adverb of frequency 'rarely' comes directly before the main verb 'attends' when there is no auxiliary verb present. 'Rarely attends' is the correct natural structure.
kept.pidgin: When no auxiliary verb dey, adverb of frequency like 'rarely' go stand before the main verb. So 'rarely attends' na the correct way to arrange am.

kept.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The baby slept ______ throughout the stormy night.
kept.explanation: The word that describes how the baby slept (a verb) must be an adverb. 'Peacefully' is the adverb form, while 'peaceful' is an adjective that cannot modify a verb.
kept.pidgin: The word wey go describe how the baby sleep (verb) must be adverb. 'Peacefully' na the adverb, but 'peaceful' na adjective wey no fit modify verb.

kept.q: Choose the option with the correct order of adjectives to complete the sentence: The village chief owns a ______ hut.
kept.explanation: The usual adjective order is age, shape, then material. 'Old' shows age, 'round' shows shape, and 'mud' shows material, so 'old round mud' follows the correct sequence.
kept.pidgin: The normal adjective order na age, shape, then material. 'Old' na age, 'round' na shape, 'mud' na material, so 'old round mud' follow the correct order.

q.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Of the two candidates interviewed for the scholarship, Tunde performed ______.
q.explanation: Since only two candidates are being compared, the comparative form 'better' should be used, not the superlative 'best'. 'More better' is grammatically wrong because 'better' already shows comparison.
q.pidgin: Since na only two candidates dem compare, na comparative 'better' we go use, no be superlative 'best'. 'More better' no correct because 'better' don already show comparison.

q.q: Choose the option that has the correct order of adverbials to complete the sentence: The students practised their drama ______ for the inter-house competition.
q.explanation: The standard order of adverbials in English is manner, then place, then time (MPT). 'Quietly' (manner), 'in the hall' (place), and 'yesterday' (time) follow this correct order.
q.pidgin: The normal order wey adverbials dey follow na manner, place, then time (MPT). 'Quietly' (manner), 'in the hall' (place), 'yesterday' (time) follow this correct order.
